title: Chords by name
summary: Name and play the I, IV and V chords in two keys, major and the minor version of one of them.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: A one-octave keyboard from middle C. C4, E4 and G4 are highlighted, the three notes of the I chord in the key of C, the first of the three chords, I, IV and V, built this week.

steps.title: Chords by name
steps.body:
Every major key has three chords that do most of the work. The I chord is built on the first note, the IV chord on the fourth, and the V chord on the fifth. Almost any simple song leans on just these three.

1. Build the I chord in your first key: the root note, the note two steps above it, and the note two steps above that.
2. Build the IV and V chords the same way, starting from the fourth and fifth notes of the same key.
3. Play all three chords in a row, naming each one out loud as you play it.
4. Repeat the same three chords in a second key, and then play the minor version of the I chord in your first key.

Once these three chords are automatic in a key, most simple songs in that key are already half-learned.

figure.alt: A two-octave keyboard from middle C. F4, A4 and C5 are highlighted, the three notes of the IV chord in the key of C, built the same way as the I chord: starting on the fourth note and stacking two more thirds on top.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: build and name I, IV and V in the first key
Sitting 2: play I, IV, V, I in a row in the first key, five times
Sitting 3: build and name I, IV and V in the second key
Sitting 4: all three chords in both keys, plus the minor I, then as if recording
An old piece played once, naming any chord you recognise

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Play I, IV and V in your first key, naming each, then play them in your second key, hands in the frame.
